name: mimalloc large-OS-page mapping backed by 2MiB pages (MAP_HUGETLB | MAP_HUGE_2MB)
component: mimalloc: unix_mmap large-page branch (Linux, mi_option_allow_large_os_pages enabled)
required_postconditions: the mapping is backed by 2MiB pages, not by the 4KiB base page - this is the entire purpose of the branch
the returned region is 2MiB-aligned, since MAP_HUGETLB forces huge-page alignment
a failure here is not an error: p == NULL falls through to the regular mmap at prim.c:390 and mimalloc runs with base pages

location.symbol: if (p == NULL) { mi_atomic_store_release(&large_page_try_ok, (size_t)8); }  (the store is on line 382)

failure_sink.description: when the huge-page mmap fails mimalloc sets large_page_try_ok to 8, which suppresses the next 8 attempts (prim.c:334-341), and then falls through to the regular mmap at prim.c:390. The allocator keeps working on 4KiB pages. Nothing is reported to the caller and nothing aborts.

source_locations.symbol: int lflags = flags & ~MAP_NORESERVE;  // using NORESERVE on huge pages seems to fail on Linux
size >= 8*large_page_size gate: mimalloc only tries large pages for allocations of at least 8 large pages (16MiB when large_page_size is 2MiB)

extraction_limitations: there is no field in this schema for 'this mapping must be backed by pages of size N'; required_page_size is documented as the page size the program has compiled into its own MMU model, which is not what MAP_HUGE_2MB expresses. It is used here because it is the only field that mentions a page size at all - the mismatch is the point of this case

the fallback mimalloc actually takes is 'the same mapping backed by smaller pages', which is not one of the FallbackKind values; smaller_size is the nearest and is still wrong (the size does not shrink)

x_campaign.rationale: rule_page_size does an equality test against the profile's page_size fact, which the probe measured as 4096, so 2097152 != 4096 fires RS-VM-0006 as Proven/Unsupported. I expect that verdict to be wrong about the program: mimalloc treats a failed huge-page mmap as a non-event and falls through to base pages at prim.c:390.
